issues.legal_issue: A party cannot reopen in the same proceedings a land-exemption issue already finally decided, or advance a ground that could have been raised before that final decision, merely because of new evidence or a later interpretation of the law.
material_facts: The landholder's original return claimed land as fuel area and rested tea area but did not claim exemption on the ground that cardamom plantation existed there.
The Supreme Court had earlier finally restored the land board's determination concerning the fuel area and rested tea area.
On remand, the landholder sought to recharacterize part of the same land as cardamom plantation and again claimed the rested tea area.
The landholder relied on later decisions and a subsequent report about the cardamom plantation, but had not amended its original return to make the cardamom claim.
issues.conclusion: The earlier final determination barred reopening the fuel-area and rested-tea issues in the same proceedings. The later cardamom claim could not be introduced on remand, and the High Court's determination on those matters was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Res judicata and estoppel, grounded in public policy and justice, apply to administrative proceedings as well as court proceedings. They prevent relitigation of an issue finally decided, including at a later stage of the same proceedings, and constructive res judicata prevents a party from raising a ground that should have been raised earlier. Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure does not exhaust the general doctrine. The Court relied on Devilal Modi v. Sales Tax Officer, Forward Construction Co. v. Prabhat Mandal, Y.B. Patil v. Y.L. Patil, and Gopal Prasad Sinha v. State of Bihar; it declined to apply the exception to issue estoppel discussed in Arnold v. National Westminster Bank. The available review powers under Section 85(9) and (9A) did not provide a basis to reopen these matters.

predicates.ceiling_proceeding_on_remand: The matter concerns a land-ceiling proceeding being considered again after remand.
predicates.prior_final_decision_on_same_land_issue: A final decision in the same proceedings determined the exemption issue concerning the land in dispute.
predicates.party_seeks_to_reopen_decided_issue: A party seeks to litigate again an exemption issue already finally decided.
predicates.party_raises_ground_that_could_have_been: A party advances a ground that could have been raised before the earlier final decision.

issues.definition: When a ceiling proceeding returns on remand after a final decision on the same land issue, a party cannot reopen that issue or rely on a ground it could have raised earlier.

issues.legal_issue: A land board's determination of interspersed agricultural land cannot exceed the extent claimed, and a supported determination within that claimed extent need not be remanded for reconsideration.
material_facts: The landholder had specifically claimed 263.83 acres as agricultural land interspersed within plantation areas.
After remand, the land board unanimously allowed that claim, considering the statutory criteria for interspersed land.
The High Court remanded the claim for fresh determination, although the land board had determined it within the extent claimed.
issues.conclusion: The determination allowing the claimed 263.83 acres was upheld, and the High Court's remand of that issue was set aside. The land board could not determine an interspersed-land area greater than the extent claimed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(44) of the Kerala Land Reforms Act includes agricultural land interspersed within plantation boundaries only to the extent determined as necessary for the protection and efficient management of plantation cultivation. The Court held that the land board's determination within the specifically claimed extent could stand because it had considered the relevant statutory factors; its authority on remand did not permit an award beyond that claim.

rule.if: plantation_ceiling_proceeding and interspersed_land_extent_claimed and board_determined_claimed_extent_as_necessary and no_failure_to_consider_relevant_factors

predicates.plantation_ceiling_proceeding: The proceeding determines the ceiling treatment of land held in connection with plantation cultivation.
predicates.interspersed_land_extent_claimed: The landholder specified an extent of agricultural land claimed as interspersed within plantation boundaries.
predicates.board_determined_claimed_extent_as_neces: The land board determined that the claimed extent was necessary for protecting and efficiently managing plantation cultivation.
predicates.no_failure_to_consider_relevant_factors: The record does not show that the land board failed to consider the relevant factors when determining the claimed extent.

issues.definition: If a land board in a plantation ceiling proceeding supports the claimed interspersed-land extent on the relevant factors, its determination within that extent stands without another remand.

issues.legal_issue: A party whose ordinary exemption claims remain barred by finality may be permitted to seek a separate discretionary exemption from the government, with an existing stay continuing while that application is decided.
material_facts: The Court upheld the final determination rejecting the landholder's claims to exemption for fuel area and rested tea area in the ceiling proceedings.
The landholder relied on later authority concerning fuel supplied to plantation employees and argued that the nature of rested tea areas had not been properly presented earlier.
The Court allowed the landholder to approach the government for a discretionary exemption and continued the existing stay until the government decided the application.
issues.conclusion: The landholder was permitted to apply to the government for a discretionary exemption, which the government was directed to decide according to law; the existing stay was to continue pending that decision.
issues.legal_principle: The Court distinguished reopening an exemption issue barred by res judicata from seeking a separate discretionary exemption from the government. It allowed an application under Section 81(3) of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, in light of the later decision in Pioneer Rubber Plantation v. State of Kerala and the contention that the rested-tea issue had not been properly presented earlier.

predicates.land_ceiling_exemption_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether land is exempt from a land-ceiling restriction.
predicates.ordinary_exemption_claim_barred_by_final: The party's ordinary claim for exemption cannot be reopened because it was finally determined earlier.
predicates.later_legal_authority_or_material_suppor: Later legal authority or material about the land provides a basis for seeking discretionary relief separately from reopening the decided claim.

issues.definition: When finality bars an ordinary exemption claim but later authority or material supports a separate discretionary request, the party may seek that relief and an existing stay continues while the request is decided.
